ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure shows a large equilateral triangle, with one white small equilateral triangle of the same size cut off at each of the three vertices, and the remaining gray region in the middle is a hexagon. The problem gives that the side length of the large equilateral triangle is 6 cm, and states that the sum of the perimeters of the three small triangles is equal to the perimeter of the gray hexagon. Reasoning: Let the side length of each small equilateral triangle be x cm. Along each side of the large triangle, a segment of length x is cut off at each of the two endpoints, so the length of the outer side segment of the gray hexagon on that side is 6 - 2x. There are 3 such outer side segments. The length of the cut side where each cut-off small equilateral triangle is adjacent to the gray hexagon is also x, and there are 3 such cut sides. Therefore the perimeter of the gray hexagon is 3(6 - 2x) + 3x. The total perimeter of the three small equilateral triangles is 3 · 3x = 9x. From the meaning of the problem, 9x = 3(6 - 2x) + 3x, that is, 9x = 18 - 3x, so 12x = 18, solving gives x = 1.5. Therefore the side length of one small triangle is 1.5 cm.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram as a large equilateral triangle with three congruent small equilateral triangles removed from its three vertices, leaving a grey hexagon. Let the side length of each small triangle be x cm. From the text, the large equilateral triangle has side 6 cm and the total perimeter of the three small triangles equals the perimeter of the grey hexagon. On each side of the large triangle, the two removed corner pieces each occupy length x, so the remaining grey outer segment on that side is 6 - 2x. The grey hexagon has three such outer segments plus three cut edges, each of length x. Thus P_hex = 3(6 - 2x) + 3x. The three little triangles together have perimeter 3 · 3x = 9x. Set 9x = 3(6 - 2x) + 3x and solve for x, giving x = 1.5 cm.

method.method_draft: First describe the picture as a large equilateral triangle whose original boundary is partly removed at all three corners, with three new straight cut edges forming the grey hexagon. Let x be the side length of each small removed equilateral triangle. From the text, the original large triangle has perimeter 3 · 6 = 18 cm. To get the grey hexagon perimeter from the original triangle perimeter, remove the six outer corner edge pieces of length x each, because each small triangle uses two sides along the original boundary. Then add back the three new cut edges, one per small triangle, each also length x. Therefore P_hex = 18 - 6x + 3x = 18 - 3x. The total perimeter of the three small triangles is 3 · 3x = 9x. Equating gives 9x = 18 - 3x, so x = 1.5 cm.
